pr_title: Save and view issue/comment content history
pr_body:
Works for issue list and pull-request list. 

Closes https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/12886 , https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/5255

Design:

1. Save issue/comment contents into a table `issue_content_history` when issues/comments are created or edited
2. Repository owner and admin can soft delete all history revisions. User can only delete his own histories
3. Guests can view public issue/comment's history revisions
4. Only 20 history revisions are kept, out-dated revisions will be delete by the order of the interval between revisions.
5. When a repository or a comment is deleted in database, related history revisions are also deleted


Screenshots:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2114189/132295206-f70d3d43-9ba0-43cc-838f-ff777d48b0ef.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2114189/132295253-df0cc757-c30b-4160-9bee-c001cda70680.png)
pr_comments:
I don't know whether enabling (hard) deletion at all is a good idea, as this feature intends to ensure data integrity and traceability.
I would say there are only two instances when you can delete the edit history of a message:
a) the message has been deleted
b) the repo has been deleted (which implies a) )

I think a better approach would be the one discussed in https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/12886#issuecomment-909724249.
That way we would still ensure data integrity after the specified time period has elapsed, while still allowing to hide small typos from the history.

> I don't know whether enabling (hard) deletion at all is a good idea, as this feature intends to ensure data integrity and traceability.
> I would say there are only two instances when you can delete the edit history of a message:
> a) the message has been deleted
> b) the repo has been deleted (which implies a) )

Yes, I just followed the logic of "DeleteComment" and "deleteIssuesByRepoID". Otherwise, user can only soft-delete a history revision (the content is updated to empty string to prevent sensitive data leaking).

> I think a better approach would be the one discussed in [#12886 (comment)](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/12886#issuecomment-909724249).
> That way we would still ensure data integrity after the specified time period has elapsed, while still allowing to hide small typos from the history.

Github saves every edited revision. It won't be a problem.

issue_context.title: Issue/comment edit history
comments:
I am conflicted about this feature:
I can totally see its value regarding data integrity and traceability.
However, I noticed that I also find it refreshing that Gitea does not track the edit history as small typos can then be deleted without a trace.

Perhaps as a compromise, there could be a set amount of time where an edit wouldn't be logged (configurable by an administrator) to allow for typographical errors to be caught and corrected.
After that, the edits would be logged as depicted above.

Just my opinion.

That sounds to me like a really good compromise.
I would suggest a timespan of 15-30 minutes as default.
(If you read through the edit history of this message, you can also already see why I think that this is a good compromise :wink: )

> That sounds to me like a really good compromise.
> I would suggest a timespan of 15-30 minutes as default.
> (If you read through the edit history of this message, you can also already see why I think that this is a good compromise 😉 )

Or the time is configuable.

Yes, but I meant as fallback if no time has been specified inside the `app.ini`.

I would definitely say that this should **only** be a server-wide setting with no further extensibility because otherwise you can have repositories where you cannot assume the validity of comments which would make this feature in my opinion less useful.
But do we really need to make it complex? GitHub just saved every change.
